newsitem.title: UK: MFI drops toward year lows on sluggish sales.
newsitem.headline: MFI drops toward year lows on sluggish sales.

text.p: Shares in MFI Furniture Group Plc fell sharply after reporting annual profits at the low end of expectations and registering modest sales in the last two months, despite a buoyant British economy, traders and analysts said.

The shares fell nine pence to 126p by 0806 GMT, approaching their year low of 120p. Some analysts said the stock, one of the most active with volume of about 5.1 million, could dip to 115, which was last touched in July 1995.
"It's very disappointing, extremely disappointing," said one retail analyst. "Given the state of the economy, profitability is very disappointing and there will be downgrades."
MFI, Britain's largest retailer and manufacturer of kitchen and bedroom furniture, said group sales edged up five percent in the first nine weeks of its current fiscal year that started on April 26.
Analysts said that not particularly impressive, given that floorcoverings group Carpetright Plc said earlier this month that its sales growth had been encouraging since the general election on May 1.

"Current year sales are relatively modest considering the economy is doing pretty well," said Robert Clark, a director at Corporate Intelligence Group. "Five percent is quite good on that score but it is not particularly startling nor is it above average for the sector. It's arguably a bit below."
Pre-tax profits of 70.3 million sterling were also at the lower end of analysts' forecasts of 70.0 to 74.5 million sterling, traders said.

"I think the market is likely to be disappointed but if you look at them in the longer term it is a bit early to tell," Clark said. "The company is in a bit of a transition that is not being fully taken into account."
